title: Garth P Probable NDE 16026
content: Here is the letter we received from him: I am a survivor. On June 5, 1998, I had my final cat scan. I then received a clean bill of health. The tumor was gone. I have something to tell you. Perhaps I should have told you before, but for some reason held back. When I was at the crest of my illness, I had a choice experience. I was oblivious to the outside world, but my inward self was active and fully conscious. My doctors were concerned at that point that I would not make it and I felt inwardly, that I was on my way out. I was spirited to a place where I saw a veil of some sort. I was allowed to penetrate that veil and on the other side beheld a different world. It was still the earth, but of such beauty, it is indescribable in many ways. The ground was covered with a matte of beautiful flowers. Their colors were brilliant and varied. There was one tree of bright green. A bright light shown all around. It was soft and penetrating, but did not hurt the eyes. I cannot adequately describe it and how it shown, but with it there was a feeling of calm and peace. Suddenly, I was jerked roughly back through the veil and returned to our world. I had an adversary. Something tore at my inner flesh and the pain was terrible, but in spite of that, I wanted to go back through the veil to the beauty I had experienced. I was allowed to go back. When I passed through the veil this time, the pain stopped. My head was bent and as I raised it, I beheld my angel wife. She was some distance from me and was on one knee picking flowers. She never spoke, but raised her head and smiled. My joy was unbounded. Her beauty filled the space. The body was not the one we buried, but the form and face of the young woman on the day we married. She was so beautiful. I started to stand with full intentions of going to her, but was again roughly jerked back though the veil and held by some unknown force. It prevented my re-entering the world of peace and beauty, but I was allowed to peer through the veil. My wife rose, smiled, and waved. She and the veil disappeared. I was left in our world of filth, smoke, and pollution. I make the comparison because of what I beheld in my wife's world. The stress in my body returned with increased vigor and pain. I looked toward heaven, pronounced my priesthood (Latter Day Saints), and cried silently for relief. The pain stopped, my outer world consciousness returned, and I realized then I was in the hospital. I tell you now, if I could have made the decision of going or staying, I would now be with my angel wife, but the Almighty must have something more for me to do. I don't know what it is, but assume he will let me know in due time. All this happened so fast as though in a few seconds or less. I may have left out some details, but you have it as I remember it. I have had one more prayer answered, I have asked continually, in my prayers to see my sweetheart just one more time. That prayer was answered. Garth P

diagnosis.severity_description: At the crest of illness; doctors concerned he would not make it
diagnosis.prognosis_given: Doctors were concerned he would not make it.
diagnosis.quality_of_life_impact: Hospitalized; at a critical point and "oblivious to the outside world"

remission_outcome.verification_detail: Final CT ("cat") scan on June 5, 1998; received a clean bill of health; "The tumor was gone."
remission_outcome.physician_quote: I then received a clean bill of health. The tumor was gone.

turner_factors.spiritual_practices_raw: Pronounced his priesthood (Latter Day Saints) and cried silently for relief; continued prayers to see his wife again.
purpose_sources: Belief that "the Almighty must have something more for me to do"
turner_factors.purpose_details: He believed he was kept alive because God had more for him to do.

pre_illness_state.loss_description: His wife had died previously ("the body was not the one we buried").

existential_shift.identity_shift_description: Shift toward spiritual framing of life/death and trust in God after the experience.
existential_shift.surrender_description: He felt he was "on my way out" and framed the outcome as God's decision/plan.
existential_shift.transformation_narrative: He described being taken beyond a veil to a peaceful, beautiful world, seeing his deceased wife, then returning and interpreting survival as God's purpose for him.
existential_shift.pivot_point_description: NDE/vision-like experience during peak illness; prayer/priesthood pronouncement followed by pain stopping and return of outer consciousness.
existential_shift.transformation_timing: Experience occurred "at the crest of my illness"; remission confirmed later by CT on June 5, 1998.

anomalous_experience.experience_description: During critical illness, he experienced passing through a veil into a beautiful world with peace/light, encountered his deceased wife, then was pulled back; after invoking LDS priesthood and crying for relief, pain stopped and he regained awareness in the hospital.
anomalous_experience.experience_timing: At the crest of his illness, while in the hospital and near death (before June 5, 1998 remission confirmation).

validation.statistical_improbability_notes: Tumor disappearance is reported, but cancer type/stage/treatment history are not provided, limiting assessment of improbability.
validation.extraction_notes: Diagnosis lacks tumor type/site/stage and treatment history; remission verification based on self-report of CT scan and 'clean bill of health' without records or named clinicians.

analysis.case_summary: A male LDS patient reports a life-threatening illness involving a tumor; during peak illness in the hospital he had a probable NDE involving passing through a veil and seeing his deceased wife. On June 5, 1998, a final CT scan reportedly showed the tumor was gone and he received a clean bill of health.
key_healing_factors: Prayer and invoking LDS priesthood for relief
Deepened spiritual meaning/purpose (belief God had more for him to do)
unique_features: Encounter with deceased spouse during the experience
Pain cessation and return of consciousness temporally linked (in narrative) to prayer/priesthood pronouncement
Remission reported as confirmed by a final CT scan with a specific date
analysis.analysis_notes: The narrative supports a medically-verified outcome only at the level of a claimed CT scan and 'clean bill of health'; no tumor type/site or conventional treatment details are provided, so remission category (pure spontaneous vs treatment-related) cannot be determined.
